   687→            op: The operation to perform.

   690→            flip: Whether to flip the order of the operation.

   692→            invoke_fn: Whether to invoke the function.
   693→

   695→            The operation result.

   709→            raise ValueError(
   710→                "flip_operands cannot be set to True if the value of 'other' operand is not provided"
   711→            )

   714→

   716→            # operand vars that are string literals need to be wrapped in back ticks.
   717→            return (
   718→                operand._var_name_unwrapped
   719→                if operand._var_is_string
   720→                and not operand._var_state
   721→                and operand._var_is_local
   722→                else operand._var_full_name
   723→            )

   726→            # check if the operation between operands is valid.
   727→            if op and not self.is_valid_operation(
   728→                types.get_base_class(left_operand._var_type),  # type: ignore
   729→                types.get_base_class(right_operand._var_type),  # type: ignore
   730→                op,

   761→                )

  1762→    def __init__(

  1793→    def __get__(self, instance, owner):

  1813→    def _deps(
  1814→        self,
  1815→        objclass: Type,
  1816→        obj: FunctionType | CodeType | None = None,
  1817→        self_name: Optional[str] = None,
  1818→    ) -> set[str]:
  1819→        """Determine var dependencies of this ComputedVar.
  1820→
  1821→        Save references to attributes accessed on "self".  Recursively called
  1822→        when the function makes a method call on "self" or define comprehensions
  1823→        or nested functions that may reference "self".
  1824→
  1825→        Args:
  1826→            objclass: the class obj this ComputedVar is attached to.
  1827→            obj: the object to disassemble (defaults to the fget function).
  1828→            self_name: if specified, look for this name in LOAD_FAST and LOAD_DEREF instructions.
  1829→
  1830→        Returns:
  1831→            A set of variable names accessed by the given obj.
  1832→        """
  1833→        d = set()
  1834→        if obj is None:
  1835→            if self.fget is not None:
  1836→                obj = cast(FunctionType, self.fget)
  1837→            else:
  1838→                return set()
  1839→        with contextlib.suppress(AttributeError):
  1840→            # unbox functools.partial
  1841→            obj = cast(FunctionType, obj.func)  # type: ignore
  1842→        with contextlib.suppress(AttributeError):
  1843→            # unbox EventHandler
  1844→            obj = cast(FunctionType, obj.fn)  # type: ignore
  1845→
  1846→        if self_name is None and isinstance(obj, FunctionType):
  1847→            try:
  1848→                # the first argument to the function is the name of "self" arg
  1849→                self_name = obj.__code__.co_varnames[0]
  1850→            except (AttributeError, IndexError):
  1851→                self_name = None
  1852→        if self_name is None:
  1853→            # cannot reference attributes on self if method takes no args
  1854→            return set()
  1855→        self_is_top_of_stack = False
  1856→        for instruction in dis.get_instructions(obj):
  1857→            if (
  1858→                instruction.opname in ("LOAD_FAST", "LOAD_DEREF")
  1859→                and instruction.argval == self_name
  1860→            ):
  1861→                # bytecode loaded the class instance to the top of stack, next load instruction
  1862→                # is referencing an attribute on self
  1863→                self_is_top_of_stack = True
  1864→                continue
  1865→            if self_is_top_of_stack and instruction.opname in (
  1866→                "LOAD_ATTR",
  1867→                "LOAD_METHOD",
  1868→            ):
  1869→                try:
  1870→                    ref_obj = getattr(objclass, instruction.argval)
  1871→                except Exception:
  1872→                    ref_obj = None
  1873→                if callable(ref_obj):
  1874→                    # recurse into callable attributes
  1875→                    d.update(
  1876→                        self._deps(
  1877→                            objclass=objclass,
  1878→                            obj=ref_obj,
  1879→                        )
  1880→                    )
  1881→                else:
  1882→                    # normal attribute access
  1883→                    d.add(instruction.argval)
  1884→            elif instruction.opname == "LOAD_CONST" and isinstance(
  1885→                instruction.argval, CodeType
  1886→            ):
  1887→                # recurse into nested functions / comprehensions, which can reference
  1888→                # instance attributes from the outer scope
  1889→                d.update(
  1890→                    self._deps(
  1891→                        objclass=objclass,
  1892→                        obj=instruction.argval,
  1893→                        self_name=self_name,
  1894→                    )
  1895→                )
  1896→            self_is_top_of_stack = False
  1897→        return d

  1904→        """
  1905→        with contextlib.suppress(AttributeError):

  1914→        hints = get_type_hints(self.fget)

  1920→def cached_var(fget: Callable[[Any], Any]) -> ComputedVar:
  1921→    """A field with computed getter that tracks other state dependencies.
  1922→

  1924→    depends on are modified.

   127→def get_attribute_access_type(cls: GenericType, name: str) -> GenericType | None:
   128→    """Check if an attribute can be accessed on the cls and return its type.
   129→
   130→    Supports pydantic models, unions, and annotated attributes on rx.Model.
   131→
   132→    Args:
   133→        cls: The class to check.
   134→        name: The name of the attribute to check.
   135→
   136→    Returns:
   137→        The type of the attribute, if accessible, or None
   138→    """
   139→    from reflex.model import Model
   140→
   141→    attr = getattr(cls, name, None)
   142→    if hint := get_property_hint(attr):
   143→        return hint
   144→    if hasattr(cls, "__fields__") and name in cls.__fields__:
   145→        # pydantic models
   146→        field = cls.__fields__[name]
   147→        type_ = field.outer_type_
   148→        if isinstance(type_, ModelField):
   149→            type_ = type_.type_
   150→        if not field.required and field.default is None:
   151→            # Ensure frontend uses null coalescing when accessing.
   152→            type_ = Optional[type_]
   153→        return type_
   154→    elif isinstance(cls, type) and issubclass(cls, DeclarativeBase):
   155→        insp = sqlalchemy.inspect(cls)
   156→        if name in insp.columns:
   157→            return insp.columns[name].type.python_type
   158→        if name not in insp.all_orm_descriptors.keys():
   159→            return None
   160→        descriptor = insp.all_orm_descriptors[name]
   161→        if hint := get_property_hint(descriptor):
   162→            return hint
   163→        if isinstance(descriptor, QueryableAttribute):
   164→            prop = descriptor.property
   165→            if not isinstance(prop, Relationship):
   166→                return None
   167→            return prop.mapper.class_
   168→    elif isinstance(cls, type) and issubclass(cls, Model):
   169→        # Check in the annotations directly (for sqlmodel.Relationship)
   170→        hints = get_type_hints(cls)
   171→        if name in hints:
   172→            type_ = hints[name]
   173→            type_origin = get_origin(type_)
   174→            if isinstance(type_origin, type) and issubclass(type_origin, Mapped):
   175→                return get_args(type_)[0]  # SQLAlchemy v2
   176→            if isinstance(type_, ModelField):
   177→                return type_.type_  # SQLAlchemy v1.4
   178→            return type_
   179→    elif is_union(cls):

   182→            type_ = get_attribute_access_type(arg, name)
   183→            if type_ is not None:

   185→                return type_
